question: What do the official Fragmenta catalogue entries actually claim about same-codex, suggested, and stylistic links among F.m.IV.156, IV.157, IV.173, Ant 99, Fr 1385, Codex 1505, and Hy 49?

iv156.access: Search-indexed official page text; direct open returned HTTP 403.
relevant_claims: The entry describes a strong stylistic resemblance to F.m.IV.157.
Codex 1505 is listed as a suggested relationship.

iv157.access: Search-indexed official page text; direct open returned HTTP 403.
relevant_claims: The entry labels CCM Ant 99 and MPO Fr 1385 as from the same codex.
It lists Turku Ms. c and MPO Codex 1505 as suggested relationships.
Its folio 8 description gives the St Olaf section with the opening-signature notation '[k] iiijr - k [v]'.

iv173.access: Official page opened directly; relevant text appeared in lines 60-72.
relevant_claims: The entry describes a wider group of at least 18 sources with uniform stylistic traits and Åbo-diocesan liturgical use.
It labels CCM Ant 242 / Fr 29666 as from the same codex, while Hy 49 / Fr 25592 and Ant 99 are suggested relationships.
It includes Codex 1505 in the broader list of related sources, not as a same-codex assertion for IV.173.

local_crosscheck.possible_alignment: The k/IV components may correspond to the F.m.IV.157 folio-8 opening-signature notation. This is an inference to test, not an established identity or join.

outcome: The published catalogue uses distinct relationship labels: same-codex, suggested, and stylistic-group membership. This clarifies prior art but establishes no new historical attribution. The possible k/IV signature alignment is a specific follow-up lead only.
limits: The direct official F.m.IV.156 and IV.157 pages returned HTTP 403 in this route; their detailed wording was available from official-page search indexing.
The relevant Taitto printed discussion on pages 161-168 and Keskiaho's 2019 chapter have not been read in full.
No local image of Fr 20278 or F.m.IV.157 was available for the proposed source-image comparison.
The k/IV correspondence has not been independently transcribed from both physical pages; no join, common hand, or same-codex relationship is inferred from it.
The frozen queue and classifications are unchanged.
